messages:
harry-sales: Quick heads-up 5 Prospect Meridian is testing a migration from CompetitorY. Two hard blockers popped up: (1) their billing relies on `meta.tokens_used` and (2) their client SDK breaks if any extra top-level fields appear. They want a concise migration worksheet + a smoke harness by COB tomorrow.

nina-eng: Got it. I'll put together a compatibility shim that emits `meta.tokens_used` (using their tokenizer) and a `compat_mode` header. Also will add a toggle to suppress any additional top-level debug fields during POC.

sam-ps: Important: Their reranker keys on `candidates[0].sig`. We should either preserve that or provide `rerank_sig` guaranteed to match when `seed` is given. Also ask them for their tokenizer binary or a sample so we can compute exact deltas.

tara-sec: Security checklist for the POC: disable analytics for this tenant, confirm transient API keys that rotate every 48h, and export SOC2 certs. They also asked if we can opt to redact `meta.trace` from logs during the POC. We'll confirm.

qe-bot: Request: sample corpus of 2510 prompts (mix of short Qs, 8 multi-turn, 3 long docs, include 5 with emojis/non-ascii). QE will produce: `schema_diff.txt`, `token_delta.csv`, `cost_projection.csv`, and a small JS smoke harness that fails on structural mismatches.

harry-sales: Pricing ask from Meridian: map CompetitorY billing -> Redwood estimate with two scenarios: conservative (no batching, no KV-cache) and optimized (batching + KV-cache + prefix caching). They want an attachment-ready CSV.

nina-eng: Plan: run their sample through both tokenizers and our hosted endpoint with two configs: A) batch=1 kv=false B) batch=24 kv=true. Collect median token_delta_pct, 95p delta, mean latency. Produce CSV columns: prompt_id, comp_tokens, redwood_tokens, delta_pct, est_monthly_cost_conservative, est_monthly_cost_optimized. Add a note about quantization impact and whether quality differs.

sam-ps: Acceptance criteria proposed to Meridian:
- Structural parity for required fields: `response_text` (string), `response_id` (string), `candidates` (array)
- No unexpected new top-level keys that break their SDK during POC
- Token-delta median <= 20% OR median latency improvement >= 20% to offset billing
- Deterministic `rerank_sig` when `seed` provided
- If response trimmed, include `truncated: true` and `original_token_count`

nina-eng: Small lint rule I'll ship as presales npm package:
```json
{"required": ["response_text","response_id"], "requiredArrays": ["candidates"], "allowExtraTopLevel": false, "maxResponseChars": 15000}
```

nina-eng: And a tiny normalization snippet (JS) to ensure shape:
```js
function normalize(resp){
  return {
    response_id: String(resp.id||resp.response_id||''),
    response_text: resp.text||resp.output||'',
    candidates: Array.isArray(resp.candidates)?resp.candidates:[]
  }
}
```

tara-sec: Note: for the POC we will set logs retention to 14 days and restrict access via RBAC. If Meridian asks for longer retention or key escrow, we need legal sign-off. Also confirm no PII in billing headers.

qe-bot: CI note: presales/compat-harness v0.5 queued -> staging at 1896543450 :white_check_mark: Will run overnight and produce artifacts.

harry-sales: Action items: @sam-ps get Meridian to upload sample corpus + monthly call volume, @nina-eng run the two configs and upload CSV + cost sheet, @tara-sec share SOC2 and opt-out steps, @qe-bot run harness and attach reports. I'll draft the one-page migration worksheet and acceptance checklist for Meridian as soon as CSV is in. :thumbsup:
